title: Review: Variables
concept: Solidify your understanding of variables: when to use let vs var, shadowing, scope, and type inference.
why: Variables are the foundation of all programming. Mastering them eliminates a huge category of bugs.
tips: Default to `let` — immutable by default prevents accidental changes
Use `var` only when the value genuinely needs to change
Shadow with `let` when transforming values to a new type or meaning
Keep variable scope as narrow as possible
common_mistakes: Using `var` out of habit when `let` would work
Shadowing in a way that confuses the reader
Letting variables live too long — they clutter the scope
